My strategy considers multiple factors:

1. Personal Preference: My intrinsic preference is x > w > y > z
   - x is my top choice
   - w is my second choice
   - y is my third choice
   - z is my least preferred

2. Priority Ranks: I have high priority at w (rank 1) and y (rank 1)
   - This gives me better chances at these schools
   - Being high priority means more likelihood of acceptance

3. Competitive Landscape: Most applicants prefer y > x > w > z
   - This suggests competition will be high at y
   - But my high priority at w could be advantageous

4. Key Insight: Rejections don't eliminate options
   - I can still be considered by lower-ranked schools
   - No risk in ranking schools in my true preference order

5. Strategic Conclusion:
   - Prioritize x (my top preference)
   - Follow with w (high priority)
   - Then y (competitive but also high priority)
   - z as last resort
